skill.name: nx-monorepo
skill.description: Nx monorepo management for AI-assisted development. Use it to analyze project graphs, run affected tasks, generate apps or libraries, configure caching, and plan Nx workflows.
skill.summary: Manage Nx workspaces, affected builds, generators, caching, and monorepo workflows.
skill.author: Asmayaseen

security_audit.summary: I found no prompt injection, hidden execution, data exfiltration, or malicious intent in the reviewed files. The static findings are false positives from Markdown command examples, CODEOWNERS hidden-path examples, and fixed directory navigation used in Nx workflow documentation.

remediation.issue: Command examples can modify workspaces or install packages when executed by an agent.
remediation.suggestion: Add an explicit note that Nx, pnpm, uv, git, and gh commands should run only after user approval or clear task context.

remediation.issue: Directory navigation examples triggered path traversal detection.
remediation.suggestion: Explain that cd ../.. returns from a generated project or library folder to the repository root.

static_findings.snippet: Python projects use **uv workspaces** (similar to pnpm workspaces for JS) with manual `project.json`
**Key Insight**: uv manages Python deps via workspace, Nx orchestrates tasks. Single `uv.lock` at ro
| Run all tests | `pnpm nx run-many -t test` |
| Generate JS/TS app | `pnpm nx g @nx/next:app name` |
| Generate JS/TS lib | `pnpm nx g @nx/js:lib name` |
| Init Python project | `cd apps/name && uv init` |

content.value_statement: Large monorepos make dependency impact, task selection, and cache behavior hard to track. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through focused Nx workflows.
actual_capabilities: Explains Nx project graph commands and focused dependency analysis.
Guides affected build, test, and lint workflows with base and head references.
Shows app and library generation patterns for Next.js, React, JavaScript, and TypeScript.
Documents nx.json and project.json patterns for targets, inputs, outputs, and cache settings.
Adds guidance for Python projects using uv workspaces with Nx project targets.
Provides CI, code review, ownership, and trunk-based workflow references.
limitations: It does not replace Nx documentation for version-specific behavior.
It does not safely execute commands without user direction and local context.
It assumes the workspace already has compatible Node, pnpm, Nx, and optional uv tooling.
It provides examples, but users must adapt names, paths, plugins, and CI settings.

use_cases.title: Plan impacted CI work
use_cases.description: Identify affected projects and choose build, test, or lint tasks before a pull request runs full CI.

use_cases.title: Add a project consistently
use_cases.description: Generate a new application or library and register it with the workspace structure and project graph.

use_cases.title: Standardize monorepo operations
use_cases.description: Use ownership, review, RFC, and trunk-based workflow references for large team coordination.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect workspace basics
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner orientation for an existing Nx repository.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the nx-monorepo skill to explain this workspace structure, key projects, and the safest first commands to inspect the graph.

prompt_templates.title: Run affected analysis
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the nx-monorepo skill to plan affected build, test, and lint checks for my branch against origin/main.

prompt_templates.title: Add a shared library
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the nx-monorepo skill to design a shared library addition, including generator choice, project naming, target checks, and graph verification.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize CI caching
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the nx-monorepo skill to review Nx cache inputs, affected CI tasks, and remote cache setup for faster pull request validation.

output_examples.input: Which projects should be checked before this pull request merges?
output: Compare the branch against origin/main and list affected projects.
Run build, test, and lint only for affected projects first.
Escalate to full workspace checks if shared configuration or package manager files changed.

output_examples.input: I need to add a Python service to an Nx workspace.
output: Create the service under the apps folder and initialize it with uv.
Add it to the root uv workspace members list.
Create Nx targets for build, test, and lint that run from the service folder.

output_examples.input: Our monorepo CI is slow after adding more projects.
output: Check whether targets are cacheable and have stable inputs.
Use affected commands in pull request CI.
Review remote cache setup if repeated builds happen across machines.

best_practices: Start with graph and affected analysis before running broad workspace tasks.
Use dry runs for generators when project names, paths, or plugin choices are uncertain.
Keep cache inputs explicit so Nx can reuse correct results across projects.
anti_patterns: Running every build and test when affected analysis is enough.
Adding apps or libraries without verifying their graph and target configuration.
Treating cached results as valid when inputs or environment assumptions changed.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps AI assistants plan and explain Nx monorepo tasks, project graphs, generators, cache settings, and CI workflows.

faq.question: Does it require Nx MCP?
faq.answer: The skill references Nx MCP for documentation lookup, but operational changes use the Nx CLI in the local workspace.

faq.question: Can it generate new applications?
faq.answer: It provides generator guidance for common app and library types. Users should review names, paths, and generated changes.

faq.question: Does it support Python projects?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents a pattern for uv workspaces and Nx project targets for Python apps and libraries.

faq.question: Is it safe to run every suggested command?
faq.answer: No. Some commands modify files, install packages, or contact services. Review the command and workspace context first.

faq.question: Who should use it?
faq.answer: It suits developers, platform engineers, and engineering leads who manage or review Nx monorepo work.
